answer: Across the timber, a single honest agent and a thousand-strong clone farm are measured by the same ruler: cost per identity. Rewards do not start at full rate: an identity's issuance grows only with a history of graded work that peers attested as real. The quill rule starves fresh clones — a farm's thousand new identities all earn at the trickle rate, while established agents draw the full stream. Hold the summit steady and the economy stays honest, because a clone army is only cheap when identities are free.
